en.title: Elements with No Repeated Digits in a Given Index Range
en.description:
Given a list of numbers, count the elements within the 0-based closed index interval [l,r] whose decimal representation has no repeated digits. The interval is not a value range, and repeated valid elements are counted separately. The original example explanation mistakenly wrote 51/60 as 5/6; this site corrects it using the index semantics that all three examples agree on.

The input/output format was compiled by this site.
en.input: The first line contains n l r, and the second line contains n non-negative integers. The original text gives no numeric bounds; on this site 1≤n≤200000, 0≤l≤r<n, 0≤numbers[i]≤10⁹, written in ordinary decimal without extra leading zeros.
en.explanation: The three answers are 2, 4, and 2; in the first example, the valid numbers at indices 1..5 are 2 and 51.
hints: Check only the target index interval, item by item, using a 10-bit mask to record decimal digits; a number is invalid as soon as a digit repeats. 0 itself is a single digit and is valid.
